s01-run-metrics.summaryMarkdown:
This is a full review at the repaired snapshot. The first review's verdict was failed and left no stored review to reattest.

**What holds:**
- **`RunMetrics` reaches every layer.** It flows through `TextRun`, `FontRun` (unresolved, which is acceptable: the derived `Hash`/`Eq` put it in all four cache keys and the scratch pool is untouched), the merge loops and `shapes_as`.
- **The shapers report per-run sizes.** CoreText maps by string index and cosmic sizes through `Attrs::metrics`. The web fallback now keeps the metrics.
- **One shared spacing/shift post-pass.** It splits shaped runs on a shift change and leaves lines without metrics unchanged.
- **Paint uses each run's size.** Strikethroughs come from the run's size and shift only.
- **Proof:** the focused groups and lane checks, plus the RayX `..Default::default()` pairing.

All five earlier findings are resolved.

s02-attributes.summaryMarkdown: Remap at the single `apply_buffer_edit` choke point is correct for every edit path (typing, platform input, IME mark/unmark/commit, paste, cut, deletes, newline, diff-scoped `rewrite_current_edit` and its rollback, undo/redo restore from history). Spans stay normalized; plain fields allocate nothing and keep the single-row splice. Typing-attribute rules, exclusive link/tag ends, IME attribute lifetime, Format history kind (never merged), Arc-shared formatting, separate format revision and `EditableTextFormatEvent` are implemented and covered by the four new groups; shaping vs paint split, metrics in `ShapeRunKey`, paint-only no-reshape and owner runs over stored paint fields hold, with the `editable-rich-attributes` scene passing lanes A, B and C. Paragraph formats and objects in `AttributedText` are planned for t11/OBJ and not required here. Both earlier findings are repaired: `set_attributed_text` maps spans through line-break normalization onto character boundaries, and `reset` leaves no typing attributes; each has a regression test in `editable_text_attributes.rs`.

s03-variable-rows.summaryMarkdown: ROW-1 and ROW-2 are met. `TextLayoutMap`'s `TextVisualRow` table (uniform rows at exact `lh*index`, mixed rows at the tallest run's scaled line height with a shared baseline, per-row `x_offset` relative to the field's alignment offset) answers paint, positions, hit testing, caret, IME bounds, selection quads, vertical/page movement, reveal, auto-scroll and the visible-row window; the widest-row bug is fixed (alignment group failed 0/3 before the fix, passes 3/3). The single-line redraw loop is resolved by comparing against the recorded requested height, with a regression test across fractional scales; `caret_bounds` now picks the run within the caret's own visual row. Focused groups pass (13 and 3 tests).

s04-paragraphs.summaryMarkdown: Repairs verified. Content width of a formatted paragraph is now the max over its rows of that row's indent (first-line indent on row 0) + width + trailing indent, and paragraph_row_x clamps an overflowing row's alignment offset at 0 so it starts at its indent; proved by `content_width_includes_each_rows_indent` (single-line field, +40 content width, row at 40, end caret revealed). update_paragraph_format steps the last paragraph back when a non-empty range ends at column 0 of a later paragraph; proved by `a_range_ending_at_a_paragraph_start_leaves_that_paragraph`. All six focused checks pass at this snapshot (paragraphs 9, alignment 5, spacing 7, lanes A/B/C). PARA-1..3 are met; the list-item field of PARA-1 is planned in s05 (t14-list-markers).

s05-lists.summaryMarkdown:
LIST-1 and LIST-2 hold at this snapshot, and the two s05 findings are resolved.

- **Enter at the start of a checked item:** the empty first half becomes the new unchecked item, and the original text stays checked, in one undo step.
- **Wide markers:** they clamp at the field's leading edge through one shared `list_marker_x`, used by marker paint, checkbox bounds and hit testing.

All five focused checks passed: lists 9, list editing 8, and lanes A, B and C.

s06-inline-objects.summaryMarkdown: OBJ-1 and OBJ-2 are met at this snapshot. The four first-review findings are resolved: the HTML-copy clause is now proved with the HTML codec in sprint 7 (CLIP-2/CLIP-3 name the object cases), a row breaks after an object, deleting a lone object no longer leaks it into typing, and only object characters skip painting in editable rows. Evidence: inline objects 11 tests, inline render 5, and lanes A, B and C for `editable-inline-objects` all pass. Note: the U+FFFC wrap candidate in `line_layout.rs` also applies to a plain U+FFFC in wrapped text, which is harmless.

findings.descriptionMarkdown: The strikethrough offset now comes from run-level size and shift only, and the split happens only at shaped-run starts. The two new `run_metrics_` tests in `line.rs` prove it.
The canvas-font remap keeps each run's metrics (`..*run`).
The sized Noop path keeps the negative descent sign. `test_platform_text_system_honors_run_sizes` asserts that an explicit line-size run equals an inherited one.
The patch-surface entry for per-run text metrics, with its test groups, was added to the closure-update checklist.

**Expected.** `set_attributed_text` replaces everything with the snapshot so that each span still covers the same characters of `AttributedText.text` (ATTR-1 'a setter that replaces everything'; d-attribute-store invariant 'spans are always normalized and within the buffer'; `AttributedText.spans` is documented as byte ranges of `text`, and it is the type the CLIP-2 HTML codec and rich paste will feed in).

**Observed.** `state.rs` `set_attributed_text` runs `normalize_input(&text.text)` (CRLF/CR become LF in multi-line fields; CR, LF and CRLF become one space in single-line fields), then builds spans with `AttributeSpans::from_spans(text.spans, replacement.len())`, which only clamps to the new length. Whenever normalization shortens the text the spans are not remapped: e.g. multi-line `AttributedText { text: "a\r\nbc", spans: [3..5 bold] }` (bold "bc") stores `3..4`, i.e. only "c" is bold; any span after a CRLF shifts right by one byte per CRLF. Neither path checks char boundaries, so a span from a caller or a shifted span can start or end inside a multi-byte character; `shape_runs_for_line` then cuts `TextRun`s mid-character and `decoration_runs` emits a mid-character run length. `attributed_text_round_trips_and_replaces_everything` only uses LF-free ASCII text.

**Repair.** In `set_attributed_text`, map each span's offsets from `text.text` to the normalized replacement (normalize while recording an old->new offset map, or reject/normalize spans through the same CRLF fold), then snap or reject span boundaries that are not char boundaries of the replacement (`is_char_boundary`) before `from_spans`. Add cases to `editable_text_attributes.rs`: CRLF text in a multi-line field, CR/LF in a single-line field, and a span boundary inside a multi-byte character.

**Resolved.** `normalize_with_offsets` (movement.rs) applies the same line-break normalization as `normalize_single_line`/`normalize_multiline` and maps every input byte offset (inside a character or CRLF pair -> start of its replacement); `set_attributed_text` maps span ranges through it before `from_spans`. Regression test `attributed_text_spans_follow_normalized_line_breaks` (CRLF+CR multi-line, CRLF+LF single-line, boundary inside a multi-byte character).

**Expected.** `reset` returns the field to a clean, plain state (history cleared; `reset_clears_formatting` asserts text typed after a reset is unformatted). The 'empty paragraph keeps its last attributes' rule (ATTR-2) is for user deletions, not for a reset.

**Observed.** `reset` calls `replace_byte_range(0..len, "")`, so `apply_edit` captures `deleted = stored_attributes(0)`; the resulting buffer is an empty paragraph, so `self.typing_attributes = Some(deleted)`. `reset` then clears history but not `typing_attributes`. If the first character was formatted (e.g. `set_attributes(0..5, bold)` on "hello world"), the next `replace_selection("new")` after `reset` is bold. The existing test passes only because its bold span starts at 2, so `stored_attributes(0)` is `None`.

**Repair.** After a successful reset clear `typing_attributes` and `composition_attributes` (or route reset through a path that skips the empty-paragraph rule). Extend `reset_clears_formatting` with a span starting at offset 0 and assert `typing_attributes().is_none()` and that text typed after the reset has no spans.

**Resolved.** `reset` now clears `typing_attributes` and `composition_attributes` after a successful reset. Regression test `reset_leaves_no_typing_attributes` (bold from offset 0; text typed after reset has no spans).

**Single-line height re-layout notifies every frame forever when the snapped bounds differ from the requested height.**

**Expected:** a single-line field asks for one extra frame only when its row height actually changed; an idle plain field schedules no frames (constraint: plain path unchanged).

**Observed:** `EditableTextPaintElement::prepaint` (element.rs, after `update_layout`) schedules `window.on_next_frame(.. cx.notify(entity_id))` whenever `line_height.max(map.size().height) != bounds.size.height`. Layout bounds are device-pixel snapped (`ToTaffy for AbsoluteLength` rounds explicit sizes, `layout_bounds_for` rounds edges), so whenever height x scale_factor is not an integer the two never match and the field re-notifies on every frame. Probe (scratch worktree with this diff, plain `"plain"` single-line field in a 400x400 div, 10 idle `advance_frame`s after settling): scale 1.0, 1.5, 2.0 -> 0 notifications; **scale 1.25 -> 10 notifications, bounds height 25.6 vs line height 26**. So every plain single-line field on a 125% display (common on Windows) redraws continuously; the same happens at any scale for a row whose height is fractional (e.g. `line_height * size/base` for a 1.17x run), and when a parent's flex constraints shrink the element. The ROW-1 single-line test only uses scale 1 with an integer doubled height, so it cannot see this.

**Repair:** compare like with like, e.g. remember the height `request_layout` last requested (in `EditableTextState` or element state) and notify only when the newly desired height differs from that requested value (or compare against `window.pixel_snap(height)` / the snapped request), never against the laid-out bounds. Add a test to `editable_text_variable_rows.rs` that settles a plain single-line field at `simulate_scale_factor_change(1.25)` and asserts no state notifications over several idle frames (and the same for a tall row with a fractional height).

**Resolution (verified):** `request_layout` records the single-line height it requests in `EditableTextState::requested_height`, and `prepaint` notifies only when `line_height.max(map.size().height)` differs from that request; snapped bounds are no longer compared. Regression test `an_idle_single_line_field_schedules_no_frames` (mirrors the reviewer's probe, which saw 10 notifications at 1.25x) asserts zero idle notifications at 1, 1.25, 1.5 and 2x for a plain field and a 1.17x run; the focused group passes 13/13.

**Expected:** in a non-wrapping field (the default single-line field, which PARA-1 says has one paragraph), every glyph of a paragraph row stays reachable: content width covers each row's indent plus width plus trailing indent, and the caret at the end of the text can be revealed by horizontal scrolling.

**Observed:** `TextLayoutMap::update` (layout_map.rs, `let indents = paragraph...`) sets `max_width = layout.width() + leading.max(0) + trailing.max(0)`, ignoring a positive `first_line_indent`, while `paragraph_row_x` places the first row at `leading + first_line_indent`. `max_scroll_offset`/reveal (state.rs ~200 and ~1472) clamp to `bounds.width - size.width`, so the last `first_line_indent` pixels of an overflowing single-line field cannot be scrolled into view. Likewise a `Center`/`Right` paragraph row wider than `available` gets `indent + editable_text_alignment_offset(..)` < indent (negative x for overflow) with no compensating `global` offset (that offset is computed from `size.width`, not from paragraph rows), so the row's start sits left of the field edge where scroll offsets (which are only <= 0) can never reach it. The non-paragraph path does not have this problem because its per-row offset and `global` cancel for the widest row.

**Repair:** compute the content width from the laid-out rows (max over visual rows of the row's indent-relative start + width + trailing indent, i.e. first row uses `paragraph_indents().0`), and clamp a paragraph row's alignment offset at its indent when the row overflows its available width (as left alignment does), or include it in the global offset. Add tests to `editable_text_paragraph_spacing.rs` / `editable_text_paragraph_alignment.rs`: a single-line field with `first_line_indent` and overflowing text whose end offset reveals fully (`max_scroll_offset` / caret visible), and a right-aligned overflowing paragraph row whose first glyph x >= its leading indent.

**Expected:** `set_paragraph_format` / `clear_paragraph_format` / `update_paragraph_format` change "the paragraphs a range touches". A non-empty range that ends exactly at the start of a paragraph (e.g. `0..4` over `"one\ntwo"`, produced by Shift+Down from a paragraph start or by selecting a paragraph with its line break) touches no character of the next paragraph, so only `one` should change (AppKit's `paragraphRangeForRange` behaves this way).

**Observed:** `update_paragraph_format` (state.rs) uses `byte_to_point(range.end).y` as the last paragraph, so `0..4` also formats `two`. The test `formats_are_set_read_and_cleared_per_paragraph` only covers ranges that end inside a paragraph or are empty.

**Repair:** for `range.end > range.start` take the last paragraph from `range.end - 1` (the paragraph of the last character in the range); keep empty ranges on the caret's paragraph. Add a case to `editable_text_paragraphs.rs` asserting that `set_paragraph_format(0..4, ..)` on `"one\ntwo"` leaves the second paragraph default.

**Expected:** Enter in a non-empty checkbox item splits it into two items; the *new* item starts unchecked and the item's existing text keeps its checked state.

**Observed:** `EditableTextState::list_insert_newline` (state.rs) always unchecks the paragraph at `caret = range.start + 1`, i.e. the second half. `Formatting::remap_paragraphs` copies the item's format to both halves. With the caret at the *start* of a non-empty checked item (e.g. `done` checked, caret at 0, Enter), the empty first half keeps `checked: true` and the original text `done` becomes `checked: false`: inserting an item above a done task un-ticks the task and leaves a ticked empty box. `a_new_checkbox_item_starts_unchecked` only covers Enter at the item's end.

**Repair:** when the split leaves the first half empty (caret at the paragraph start and the selection does not reach into the previous paragraph), uncheck the first paragraph (`range.start`) instead of the second, so the original text keeps its state. In general, the new item is the half that does not hold the original text start. Add a case to `editable_text_list_editing.rs`: checked `done`, caret at 0, Enter, then expect `[Checkbox{checked:false}, Checkbox{checked:true}]`, text `\ndone`, and one undo step back.

**Resolved:** the fix is in `list_insert_newline`. When the character before the split is none or a break, it unchecks the empty first half (`range.start`); otherwise it unchecks the second half. Either way the change is made inside the same undo step. The regression test is `enter_at_the_start_of_a_checked_item_keeps_its_state`.

**Expected:** the marker paints right-aligned *in the space before* the item's first row.

**Observed:** the marker origin is `start.x - 0.4*font_size - line.width` (element.rs prepaint) with no lower bound. With the default 24 px step at level 0, the space is 24 px. At 16 px, the gap alone takes 6.4 px. So `10.` (about 20 to 29 px depending on the font) and even `1.` in a monospace font like Lilex (19.2 px) end up at a negative x, left of the field's content edge, where they are clipped or overlap whatever is beside the field. Larger first-character sizes make this worse. The `editable-lists` scene uses a 40 px step, and no unit test checks the marker's left edge for numbers, so nothing exercises this.

**Repair:** keep the marker inside the item's leading space. For example, clamp its left edge to the paragraph's content start (`max(0, …)` in content coordinates) and let it reduce the gap. Or record in the design that wide markers may extend past the indent. Then add a test in `editable_text_lists.rs` with a level-0 item numbered 10+ at the default step that asserts where the marker's left edge sits.

**Resolved:** the new `TextLayoutMap::list_marker_x` clamps the marker's x at the field's leading edge (`-alignment_offset`, using the same inputs as the geometry's offset). Both `list_checkbox_bounds` (and so hit testing) and element marker painting use it. The regression test is `wide_markers_stay_inside_the_field`.

**Expected (OBJ-1):** HTML copy writes each object's HTML fallback, or else its escaped text fallback, proved in `editable_text_inline_objects.rs`.

**Observed:** `InlineObject::html_fallback` is stored but nothing reads it. `copy()` (state.rs) writes only `ClipboardItem::new_string(plain_text)`; there is no HTML entry, codec or test. The HTML clipboard (CLIP-1), codec (CLIP-2, which already lists "objects as their HTML fallback, or escaped text fallback") and rich copy (CLIP-3) belong to s07, so this OBJ-1 clause cannot be met in s06 as written.

**Repair:** amend the specs so the clause is owned where it can be proved: move "HTML copy writes its HTML fallback, or else its escaped text fallback" out of OBJ-1 into CLIP-2/CLIP-3 (with explicit cases in `editable_text_html.rs` for an object with and without `html_fallback`, the latter escaping `<`/`&` in the text fallback, and in `editable_text_rich_clipboard.rs` for copy of a selection holding an object). Alternatively record a user-decided deferral disposition for that clause. Re-review OBJ-1 after the amendment.

**Resolution (verified):** specification revision 79 keeps the HTML-copy clause in OBJ-1 and states that it is proved with the HTML codec: an object with and without an HTML fallback in `editable_text_html.rs` (CLIP-2) and `editable_text_rich_clipboard.rs` (CLIP-3), whose criteria now name the object cases. Sprint 7 owns that proof; the final review must confirm those cases exist.

**Expected (OBJ-1, d-inline-objects):** "a row may break before or after it"; wrapping treats the object as an unbreakable word.

**Observed:** wrap boundaries for rows with objects come from `LineLayout::compute_wrap_boundaries_with` (line_layout.rs ~303). U+FFFC is not a `LineWrapper::is_word_char`, so it is a candidate *before* itself, but a following word character only becomes a candidate after a space (`prev_ch == ' '`). There is no break opportunity after an object followed directly by text. Example (200 px field, ~9.6 px glyphs, 40 px object): `"aa \u{FFFC}" + 20×'b'`. Breaking after the object would give rows `aa ￼` / `bbbb…` (192 px fits). Observed: the break falls before the object (`aa ` / `￼bbbb…`), and since `￼bbbb…` is 232 px with no further candidate, the b-word is force-split mid-word into a third row. The test group only proves the break *before* an object (`an_object_never_splits_and_a_row_may_break_before_it`).

**Repair:** make the position right after an inline object a wrap candidate (e.g. in the editable layout's wrap step, or in `compute_wrap_boundaries_with` treat `prev_ch == '\u{FFFC}'` as a candidate, recording the gpux-local patch in the closure-update checklist since line_layout.rs is a Zed closure file), and add a test `a_row_may_break_after_an_object` to `editable_text_inline_objects.rs` with the example above, proved failing on the current code.

**Resolution (verified):** `compute_wrap_boundaries_with` treats a word character after U+FFFC as a wrap candidate, as after a space. The closure-update checklist records the gpux patch. Regression `a_row_may_break_after_an_object` (rows `aa ￼` / 16 b's); the coordinator reports it failed with the change reverted (row 0 was 0..3).

**Expected (OBJ-1 editing, `TextAttributes::object` doc "Typing never takes it"):** text typed where an object was never carries the object attribute.

**Observed:** in `apply_edit_then` (state.rs ~1812-1832), a deletion that leaves its paragraph empty sets `typing_attributes = Some(self.stored_attributes(range.start))`, and `stored_attributes` returns the span's attributes unchanged, object included. `insertion_attributes` returns explicit typing attributes before its new `without_object` stripping. Scenario: text `\u{FFFC}` (object alone in its paragraph), caret after it, `delete_backward`, then type `x` -> `attributes_at(0).object == Some(chip)`; the span on `x` and `AttributedText.spans` carry the object (and a later owner HTML/serialization of spans sees it).

**Repair:** strip the object when saving deleted attributes for the empty paragraph (e.g. store `deleted.without_exclusive()`-like value with `object: None`, keeping link/tag behaviour as today), and add a case to `attribute_changes_keep_objects_and_typing_never_takes_them` (or a new test) deleting a lone object then typing.

**Resolution (verified):** `apply_edit_then` saves `without_exclusive()` attributes when the deleted character carried an object. Regression `typing_after_deleting_a_lone_object_takes_no_object`.

**Expected:** only an inline object's character goes unpainted (the task notes "rows-mode paint skips the U+FFFC glyph"); plain text paths are unchanged.

**Observed:** the skip is in the shared `paint_line` (line.rs ~902), used by `ShapedLine::paint`, `WrappedLine::paint`, the rows-mode paths and the fast-mode path alike. Every U+FFFC in any `Text`/`StyledText`/label, and a U+FFFC typed or pasted into an editable field without an object attribute, now reserves its glyph advance but paints nothing (it used to paint the font's glyph). It also adds a per-glyph byte comparison to the hottest text paint loop for all text.

**Repair:** limit the skip to editable rows painting objects: pass the row's object offsets (or a flag set only when the row has objects) from `EditableTextPaintElement` into `paint_rows`, and skip only those glyph indices; add a test that a plain U+FFFC without an object attribute still paints.

**Resolution (verified):** `paint_line` takes `hidden_glyphs`; every caller passes `&[]` except `WrappedLine::paint_rows` from the editable element, which passes `logical_row_object_offsets(row)` (only characters carrying an object attribute, in the same display-line coordinates as glyph indices). Other text paints U+FFFC as before, and the empty-slice check keeps the plain loop cost unchanged. Regression `a_plain_replacement_character_is_not_an_object` proves a typed U+FFFC is no object and gets no box; the paint side holds by construction (empty offsets).
